findings.title: checkIfIsAvailable skips busy-time check when a date override exists
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, if a date override exists for the slot's date and the slot falls within the override window, `dateOverrideExist` is set to `true` and lines 133-135 immediately `return true` before running `busy.every(...)` at line 153. As a result, any existing bookings or calendar busy times on a day with a date override are completely ignored, allowing double-bookings during date override hours.

findings.title: Dayjs object reference comparison with === is always false and boundary conditions are off
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, line 114 compares two newly constructed Dayjs instances using `===` (`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")`), which compares object references and is always `false`; `.isSame(...)` must be used to detect zero-length (unavailable-all-day) overrides. Additionally, lines 118-125 reject a slot when `slotEndTime <= overrideStart` or `slotStartTime > overrideEnd`, instead of checking whether the slot `[slotStartTime, slotEndTime]` is not fully contained within `[overrideStart, overrideEnd]` (i.e. `slotStartTime.isBefore(overrideStart) || slotEndTime.isAfter(overrideEnd)`). A slot that starts before the override begins (but ends after `overrideStart`) or starts before `overrideEnd` (but ends after `overrideEnd`) will be treated as valid.

findings.title: Working hours check in checkIfIsAvailable uses slotStartTime for end and rejects multi-range schedules
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable` lines 138-151: (1) `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` uses `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so a slot whose end extends past `workingHour.endTime` is not caught; and (2) `workingHours.find(...)` returns `true` (causing `checkIfIsAvailable` to return `false`) as soon as *any* workingHour entry for that day does not contain the slot. If a user has split working hours on the same day (e.g., 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00) or multiple entries for a day, a slot in the afternoon will fail against the morning entry and be falsely rejected.

findings.title: Date override timezone shift can cross midnight or fail activeOverrides filter
findings.body: In `getSlots` (`packages/lib/slots.ts`), `activeOverrides` (lines 206-208) filters `dateOverrides` by checking if `dayjs.utc(override.start)` (which stores the organizer's local wall-clock time as UTC) falls within `[startOfInviteeDay, startOfInviteeDay.endOf("day"))`. When the invitee and organizer are in different timezones, an override on day D in the organizer's timezone can fall on day D-1 or D+1 in the invitee's timezone, or `override.start` (as raw UTC) may lie outside `[startOfInviteeDay, endOf("day"))`. Furthermore, lines 218-223 compute `startTime` and `endTime` using `.add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + ...`, which wraps around modulo 1440 when `override.start + offset` crosses midnight UTC, producing inverted or wrong minute-of-day bounds (e.g. `startTime > endTime`).
